Cryptic

/KRIP-tik/ — rhymes with mystic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cryptic describes something whose meaning is mysterious or hard to figure out, as if written in a puzzle on purpose.

Her cryptic reply — 'ask the clock' — puzzled us for days.

Worked Example

The treasure map was covered in cryptic symbols that only the original pirate understood, forcing modern hunters to decode every mark like pieces of a puzzle.

Cryptic emphasizes that the meaning is hidden ON PURPOSE and requires figuring out — it's not just unclear or vague, it's deliberately obscure like a puzzle. That deliberate mystery is what makes cryptic more precise than 'unclear.'

How Cryptic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

mysterious

mysterious: strange and difficult to explain

obscure

obscure: with meaning hidden from easy understanding

vague

vague: expressed in an indefinite, unclear way

Antonyms

explicit

explicit: spelling everything out, hiding nothing

straightforward

straightforward: direct and instantly easy to follow

How Strong Is It? — puzzling → enigmatic → incomprehensible → cryptic

puzzling vs. cryptic

puzzling vs. cryptic: Puzzling is milder than cryptic — a puzzling note is confusing by accident, while a cryptic one seems designed to hide its meaning like a riddle.

enigmatic vs. cryptic

enigmatic vs. cryptic: Enigmatic is a shade stronger than cryptic: a cryptic clue can be cracked with effort, but an enigmatic one stays mysterious even after long study.

incomprehensible vs. cryptic

incomprehensible vs. cryptic: Incomprehensible is the far end beyond cryptic — a cryptic message tempts you to decode it, while an incomprehensible one cannot be understood at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — crypt

Root — crypt: hidden (Greek kryptos, from kryptein, 'to hide') (Greek)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: relating to, characteristic of (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Crypt ('hidden') + -ic ('relating to') literally means 'of the hidden' — a cryptic message keeps its meaning buried, forcing you to dig for it as if it were a coded riddle.

Use the root in a new word: crypt

Use the root in a new word: crypt: A crypt is a hidden underground chamber beneath a church — the same Greek kryptos, 'hidden,' that makes a cryptic message hide its meaning from the reader.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Cryptic is used for meanings that are intentionally hidden or puzzle-like, not just unclear or poorly explained. Use it when you want to emphasize the deliberate mystery or code-like quality. For something just hard to understand, 'unclear' or 'confusing' works, but cryptic specifically means you need to decode it.
